questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Unit Tangent Vector at a Given Point
questions.problem: What is the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,k$ at the point $P(2\pi ,1,0)?$
questions.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)\,j+y(t)\,j+z(t)\,k$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by 

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find the value of $t$ that corresponds to the point $P(2\pi ,1,0)$ on the given curve. We know that

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =2\pi \,i+\,j+0\,k \\ t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,k & =2\pi \,i+\,j+0\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the respective components gives the system

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}t=2\pi  \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡t=1 \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡t=0.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equality, $t=2\pi .$ This value also satisfies the other two equations. Therefore, the point $P(2\pi ,1,0)$ is at the tip of $r(2\pi ).$  

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=2\pi :$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,k \\  & =i-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,k \\ {r}^{′}(2\pi ) & =\,i-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi )\,j+\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi )\,k \\  & =i+0\,j+\,k \\  & =i+k\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(2\pi ):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(2\pi )‖ & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+0+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(2\pi )$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the given curve at $P(2\pi ,1,0):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}T(2\pi ) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(2\pi )}{‖{r}^{′}(2\pi )‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot (i+k) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,i+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: What is the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=t\,i+{t}^{2}\,j+2{t}^{2}\,k$ at the point $P(2,4,8)?$
questions.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)\,j+y(t)\,j+z(t)\,k$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find the value of $t$ that corresponds to the point $P(2,4,8)$ on the given curve. We know that

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =2\,i+4\,j+8\,k \\ t\,i+{t}^{2}\,j+2{t}^{2}\,k & =2\,i+4\,j+8\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the respective components gives the system

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}t=2 \\ {t}^{2}=4 \\ 2{t}^{2}=8.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equality, $t=2.$ This value also satisfies the other two equations. Therefore, the point $P(2,4,8)$ is at the tip of $r(2).$ 

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{2})\,k \\  & =i+2t\,j+4t\,k \\ {r}^{′}(2) & =\,i+2\cdot 2\,j+4\cdot 2\,k \\  & =i+4\,j+8\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(2)‖ & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{4}^{2}+{8}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{81} \\  & =9\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(2)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the given curve at $P(2,4,8):$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(2) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(2)}{‖{r}^{′}(2)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{9}\cdot (i+4\,j+8\,k) \\  & =\frac{1}{9}\,i+\frac{4}{9}\,j+\frac{8}{9}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: What is the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=⟨4t,\,4\operatorname{ln}⁡t,\,{t}^{2}⟩$ at the point $P(4,0,1)?$
questions.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),y(t),z(t)⟩$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find the value of $t$ that corresponds to the point $P(4,0,1)$ on the given curve. We know that

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨4,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ ⟨4t,\,4\operatorname{ln}⁡t,\,{t}^{2}⟩ & =⟨4,\,0,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the respective components gives the system

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}4t=4 \\ 4\operatorname{ln}⁡t=0 \\ {t}^{2}=1.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equality, $t=1.$ This value satisfies the other two equations. Therefore, the point $P(4,0,1)$ is at the tip of $r(1).$  

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=1:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4\operatorname{ln}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨4,\,\frac{4}{t},\,2t⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(1) & =⟨4,\,\frac{4}{(1)},\,2(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨4,\,4,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(1)‖ & =\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{4}^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{36} \\  & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(1)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the given curve at $P(4,0,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(1) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(1)}{‖{r}^{′}(1)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}⟨4,\,4,\,2⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{2}{3},\,\frac{2}{3},\,\frac{1}{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding Unit Tangent Vectors Using the Rules of Differentiation For Vector Functions
questions.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)={t}^{2}p(t)$ at the point corresponding to $t=1$, given that  $p(1)=i-\,j-k\,$ and $\,{p}^{′}(1)=-i+\,j+\,k.$
questions.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j+z(t)k$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=1:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}p(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})\cdot p(t)+{t}^{2}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(p(t)) \\  & =2t\,p(t)+{t}^{2}\,{p}^{′}(t) \\ {r}^{′}(1) & =2(1)\,p(1)+(1)^{2}\,{p}^{′}(1) \\  & =2(i-\,j-k)+(-i+\,j+\,k) \\  & =2i-2\,j-2k-i+j+\,k \\  & =i-j-k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(1):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}‖r(1)‖ & =\sqrt{(1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(1):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}T(1) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(1)}{‖{r}^{′}(1)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\cdot (i-j-k) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}(i-j-k)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the unit tangent vector to the curve at the point that corresponds to $t=1$ is  $T(1)=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}(i-j-k).$

questions.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=({t}^{2}-2t)p(t)$ at the point corresponding to $t=1$, given that  $p(1)=i+2\,j-k\,$ and $\,{p}^{′}(1)=2\,i-\,j-2\,k.$
questions.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j+z(t)k$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=1:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(({t}^{2}-2t)p(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-2t)\cdot p(t)+({t}^{2}-2t)\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(p(t)) \\  & =(2t-2)\,p(t)+({t}^{2}-2t)\,{p}^{′}(t) \\ {r}^{′}(1) & =(2(1)-2)\,p(1)+((1)^{2}-2(1))\,{p}^{′}(1) \\  & =0-{p}^{′}(1) \\  & =-(2\,i-\,j-2\,k) \\  & =-2i+\,j+2k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(1):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}‖r(1)‖ & =\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+(1)^{2}+(2)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(1):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}T(1) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(1)}{‖{r}^{′}(1)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot (-2\,i+j+2k) \\  & =-\frac{2}{3}\,i+\frac{1}{3}\,j+\frac{2}{3}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the unit tangent vector to the curve at the point that corresponds to $t=1$ is  $T(1)=-\frac{2}{3}\,i+\frac{1}{3}\,j+\frac{2}{3}\,k.$
